You make a good argument, but I think you are missing the point. Humans are adaptable, conventional machines and programs are not. An automated lift can take the job of a lift boy, but it can't fly a plane. The historic pattern is: Specialized and cheap automation forces adaptable and expensive workers into new jobs. What's happening now, however, is not a continuation of this pattern, it's a break of the pattern. AI is capable of learning and specializing very quickly. There's still room for human labor as things stand right now, but AI is advancing rapidly and so is robotics. It's entirely plausible that AI systems can take many jobs without the workers being able to move on to new jobs because these will be taken by AI as well.
Shane Stanley tells it as it is. Essentially he is underscoring the old saying: Chance/luck happens when opportunity meets the prepared mind.

@16:05 Avid was the pioneer for film editing. Nobody in the film or broadcast video business used Adobe Premiere, which came out after Avid. Premiere was a prosumer product used for cheesy CD-Rom videos and web 1.0 videos. Film and television almost exclusively used Avid for NLE, or in rare cases a pro competitor like Media100 or Lightworks. It wasn't until the late 2000s when professionals started moving away from Avid and started using Final Cut Pro, Premiere Pro, etc.

Essentially you're betting that the capacity increases in AI plateau below the threshold of human relevance either in general or at least for specific roles that humans want to continue to exist in. I don't think you've made any argument for why you think that's the case. You're largely looking at what's possible now, in which case I think you'd find few people who would disagree with you. If you look at current and historical trends, I think there's a lot of reason to think that AI will obsolete humans (first economically, then culturally, finally existentially), full stop. The issue (probably) isn't whether humans (as we know ourselves today) go away, it's how? What does that look like as it plays out?
